claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion is controlled by the ability to rapidly form and repair a dense, nanostructured oxide/tribolayer.
A nanocrystalline or amorphous near-surface microstructure enhances the formation and stability of a protective film during combined mechanical and corrosive attack.
Thermal shock or targeted microalloying can induce the proposed nanocrystalline or amorphous near-surface state.
The engineered near-surface state promotes rapid oxide/tribolayer formation.
The engineered nanocrystalline or amorphous surface layer facilitates rapid dynamic repassivation.
The engineered surface layer facilitates formation of a continuous protective oxide/tribolayer.
After mechanical disruption, the protective oxide/tribolayer rapidly reforms and heals.
Rapid film healing reduces particulate loss from mechanical wear.
The protective film limits electrolyte access to the underlying alloy.
The tailored surface microstructure enables continuous regeneration of the protective layer under dynamic tribocorrosion conditions.
The treated HEA will have a lower wear rate than the matched baseline.
The treated HEA will have a lower corrosion current density than the matched baseline.
Interaction between wear and corrosion will produce less-than-additive combined degradation in the treated HEA.
The predicted advantage holds when the applied wear rate remains low enough for effective repassivation.
An excessively high wear rate will diminish or eliminate the advantage of the modified surface.
A chemical environment that inhibits oxide formation will diminish or eliminate the advantage of the modified surface.
